title: Historical and polity traditions admitted — none for faith dogmas or morals
source_text: XXXVIII. Itaque non omnino quidem contemnimus, & rejicimus traditiones non scriptas circa res historicas, & Ecclesiarum ritus, ordinem, atque politiam: sed tamen nullas admittimus circa fidei dogmata, & ea quae ad mores pertinent. Neque putamus illa quae Spiritus non judicavit opus esse scripto mandari per suos amanuenses Apostolos & Evangelistas, tanta certitudine a nobis sciri posse, aut eandem authoritatem in Ecclesia habere, ac illa quae scriptis voluit consignari, ut aeternae legis vim in Ecclesia haberent.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore we do not altogether despise and reject unwritten traditions concerning historical matters and the rites, order, and polity of the Churches: but nevertheless we admit none concerning the dogmas of faith and those things which pertain to morals. Nor do we think that those things which the Spirit did not judge needful to be committed to writing through his amanuenses the Apostles and Evangelists can be known by us with so great certainty, or have the same authority in the Church, as those which he willed to be consigned in writing, so that they might have the force of an eternal law in the Church.
pass_b_english: We do not wholly despise or reject unwritten traditions about historical matters and the Churches' rites, order, and polity.

But we admit none for the dogmas of faith, or for what belongs to morals. What the Spirit did not judge needful to put in writing through his amanuenses the Apostles and Evangelists cannot be known by us with equal certainty, or hold equal authority in the Church, as what he willed to consign in writing to have the force of an eternal law there.

choices.why: Keep technical term for Spirit's writers.
